newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai police freeze Khashoggi's shares in firm.
newsitem.headline: Thai police freeze Khashoggi's shares in firm.

text.p: Thai police said on Wednesday they had frozen shares worth 142 million baht ($5.5 million) held by Saudi tycoon Adnan Khashoggi in local firm Jalaprathan Cement Plc.
An arrest warrant was issued last week by Thai police for Khashoggi who is wanted here on charges of conspiring to defraud ailing local bank Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc.

"I have received a report from the economic crime investigation police that they have ordered the freezing of the shares of Adnan Khashoggi worth 142 million baht in Jalaprathan Cement Plc," Thai police chief, Pracha Promnok, told reporters.
Trading in shares of Jalaprathan were suspended earlier on Wednesday by the Thai bourse pending more details from the firm on details of a proposed capital increase.

The arrest warrant for Khashoggi, and four other officials of the troubled bank, was issued on a request by the Thai central bank on suspicion that they jointly conspired for Khashoggi to draw two billion baht in loans from Bangkok Bank of Commerce without credible collateral in 1995.
Khashoggi, 61, said in published remarks on Sunday that he was preparing a response to the Thai charges and was hopeful of an amicable settlement.
